<h2 id="sheets"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#sheets">Sheets</a></h2>
<p>Ask a question and Grok answers from the spreadsheet itself, citing the cells it used. It writes and fills formulas, inserts charts, and reruns scenarios when an assumption changes, so updating a model no longer means rebuilding it. Every change is a normal edit you can check and undo.</p>
<h2 id="slides"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#slides">Slides</a></h2>
<p>Grok turns an outline into a working presentation, researching from the web or X and adding diagrams or images where they help. It extends a deck in its existing theme and rewrites titles so each slide makes its point. The result is regular, editable slides, not an export to fix up.</p>
<h2 id="docs"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#docs">Docs</a></h2>
<p>Grok writes where the writing happens. It turns rough notes into a structured draft with real headings and lists, fixes grammar in place, and keeps style consistent across a long file. With <a href="https://grok.com/connectors" target="_blank">connectors</a> enabled, it can pull from recent emails or files in Google Drive.</p>
<h2 id="get-started"><a class="heading-anchor" href="#get-started">Get started</a></h2>
<p>Grok for Google Workspace is a free add-on, and one install from the <a href="https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/grok/660927092109" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Google Workspace Marketplace</a> covers Sheets, Slides, and Docs. Also available for Microsoft 365 in <a href="/grok/word">Word</a>, <a href="/grok/excel">Excel</a>, <a href="/grok/powerpoint">PowerPoint</a>, and <a href="/grok/outlook">Outlook</a>.</p>
